# Facilitator Session Guide — The Specialist Walkthrough Lens

> **Read `_facilitator-conventions.md` first**, and the F2 calibration session (`../leaders/session-observer-calibration-f2.md`) — the Specialist lens uses the same rubric discipline.

---

## Why this session exists

Eduversal Subject Specialists visit partner schools for appraisal-visit walkthroughs (typically 1–2 visits a year, plus a 10-walkthrough development cycle across the year). On these visits, a Specialist watches lessons in their subject and gives feedback. Two risks:

1. **The lens drifts by subject.** A Maths Specialist and an English Specialist may judge "good teaching" differently — but the appraisal rubric is the same across subjects. The Specialist must hold the shared lens *and* add genuine subject expertise on top.
2. **Feedback stays general.** A Specialist's value is subject-specific insight ("your worked example skipped the step where Year 8 students always trip"). General feedback any leader could give wastes the visit.

This session prepares Specialists to observe through the **shared appraisal lens**, add **subject-specific depth**, and connect what they see to the **teacher competency framework** — consistently across every school.

---

## Learning objectives

By the end of this session, each Specialist can:

1. **Observe** a lesson using the F2 rubric, the same way every observer should (calibrated).
2. **Add** subject-specific feedback that only a subject expert could give.
3. **Connect** a walkthrough finding to a teacher competency and a next step.
4. **Hold** the same lens across schools and subjects, so the network is consistent.

---

## What the Specialist lens draws on (facilitator background)

- **The shared appraisal lens** — F2 (Class Observation), the same 45-item rubric leaders use (`appraisal-framework-v2.json → F2`). The Specialist is calibrated to it like any observer.
- **The specialists competency framework** — 6 domains (`competency_framework/specialists`): **CSM** Cambridge Subject Mastery, **COF** Classroom Observation & Feedback, **TPD** Teacher Professional Development, **CQA** Curriculum & Quality Assurance, **NLS** Network Leadership & Strategy, **XEN** External Expertise & Network. The walkthrough lens lives mostly in CSM + COF.
- **The teacher competency framework** — what the Specialist connects findings *to*, so feedback points a teacher toward a growth step, not just a judgement (`competency_framework/teachers`).
- **The Charter** — walkthrough notes are confidential and developmental; a development walkthrough is NOT an appraisal score (Charter NN1 spirit — keep development and evaluation separate).

> **Words used here:** **F2** = the class-observation part of the teacher appraisal. **Walkthrough** = a short, structured classroom visit. **Calibrated** = scoring the same way as other observers, against the written rubric.

---

## Run-of-show (120 minutes)

| Time | Block | Facilitator does | Participants do | Slide |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:12 | **Welcome & frame** | Frame the Specialist's unique value: subject depth on top of the shared lens. | Name one subject-specific thing only a Specialist would notice. | 1–3 |
| 0:12–0:30 | **Input: the shared lens** | Walk F2 + the calibration discipline. Specialists score the rubric like any observer. | Follow the F2 rubric. | 4–7 |
| 0:30–0:42 | **Input: adding subject depth** | Show the difference between general feedback and subject-expert feedback. | Compare two feedback examples. | 8–9 |
| 0:42–1:06 | **Activity 1 — observe + score** | Specialists watch a subject vignette/video, score 2–3 F2 items, AND note one subject-specific observation. | Score + add subject note. | 10 |
| 1:06–1:24 | **Activity 2 — connect to competency** | For one finding, connect it to a teacher competency + a concrete next step. | Map finding → competency → step. | 11 |
| 1:24–1:40 | **Debrief** | Surface: did the lens stay consistent? Did the subject depth add real value? | Share one subject-specific insight. | 12–13 |
| 1:40–1:52 | **Consistency across schools** | How to hold the same lens in School A and School B. The confidentiality of development walkthroughs. | Discuss. | 14 |
| 1:52–2:00 | **Close** | Exit ticket. Link to the train-the-trainer non-negotiables. | Write exit ticket. | 15 |

## Facilitator talking points

**On the shared lens first.** *"Before you add your subject expertise, you score the lesson the same way every observer does — against the F2 rubric, on evidence. Your subject knowledge does not replace the rubric; it sits on top of it."* (`appraisal-framework-v2.json → F2`).

**On subject depth (the Specialist's real value).** Show the difference:
- **General (any leader could say):** *"Your explanation could be clearer."*
- **Subject-expert (only a Specialist could say):** *"When you introduced negative indices, you skipped the bridge from 'repeated division' — that is exactly where Year 8 students form the 'minus means subtract' misconception. Show the division pattern first."*

*"That second comment is why we send a Subject Specialist. It is precise, it is subject-specific, and the teacher can act on it tomorrow. Aim for that."* (`competency_framework/specialists → csm`, Cambridge Subject Mastery).

**On connecting to competency.** *"A finding is more useful when it points somewhere. 'Your questioning stayed at recall level' is a judgement. 'Your questioning stayed at recall — the next step is higher-order questioning, which is LCP-3 in the teacher framework; here is one technique to try' is development."* (`competency_framework/teachers`).

**On confidentiality and the Charter.** *"A development walkthrough is not an appraisal score. Keep the two separate. Your walkthrough notes help the teacher grow; they do not feed a grade. This protects the honesty that makes teachers open to you."* (Charter NN1 spirit — development firewalled from evaluation).

**On consistency across schools.** *"You visit many schools. The lens must be the same in each one. A '3' in School A is a '3' in School B. Calibrate with the other Specialists — the same way leaders calibrate within a school."*

---

## Activity instructions

### Activity 1 — Observe, score, add subject depth (24 min)
Specialists watch a subject lesson (video or vignette). They:
1. Score **2–3 F2 items** against the rubric (the shared lens).
2. Write **one subject-specific observation** that only a subject expert would make.

### Activity 2 — Connect to competency (18 min)
For one of their findings, each Specialist writes:
- The finding (with lesson evidence).
- The **teacher competency** it connects to (from `competency_framework/teachers`).
- One **concrete next step** the teacher could take.
- One **subject-specific resource or technique** to support it.

- **Online:** breakout rooms by subject, so subject depth can be compared.

> **Why this works:** Specialists practise the full move — score consistently, add depth, point to growth. That is the whole value of a Specialist visit in one exercise.

---

## Common questions (answer in simple English)

**"Do I score the lesson like an appraisal?"**
You use the same F2 rubric and the same evidence discipline. But a *development* walkthrough is for growth, not for a grade. Keep development separate from formal appraisal scoring.

**"What if my subject judgement and the rubric disagree?"**
Score the rubric on evidence first. Then add your subject insight as feedback. The rubric keeps you consistent with other observers; your expertise adds the subject depth on top.

**"How is the specialists framework different from the teacher one?"**
The teacher framework is about *teaching*. The specialists framework is about *supporting teaching across the network* — subject mastery, observation & feedback, developing teachers, quality assurance. You grow in yours while helping teachers grow in theirs.

**"How do I stay consistent with other Specialists?"**
Calibrate together, the same way leaders do — score the same lesson and reconcile by the rubric. And hold the train-the-trainer non-negotiables on every visit.

---

## Exit ticket

1. One way I will add subject depth on my next visit.
2. One thing I will do to stay consistent with other Specialists.
3. One thing I am still unsure about.

> Collect line 3 — it shows the Director where the Specialist team needs alignment before the visit season.
